statement.p: The form of the partial fraction decomposition of a rational function is given below.

solution.p: Multiplying by the least common denominator gives 2x-2x^{2}-26 = A(x^2+9)+(Bx+C)(x - 4) Rearranging terms on the right hand side, yields 2x-2x^{2}-26 = (A+B)x^2+(-4B+C)x + 9 A - 4C Now we equate the coefficients: \begin{array}{rl} A+B \amp = -2 \\ -4B +C \amp = 2 \\ 9 A - 4C \amp = -26 \end{array} Solving the system gives A=-2, \; B = 0 and C= 2 so the partial fraction decomposition is \frac{2x-2x^{2}-26}{(x - 4)(x^2+9)} = \frac{-2}{x - 4} + \frac{2}{x^2+9} The definite integral is then \displaystyle \int \frac{2x-2x^{2}-26}{(x - 4)(x^2+9)} dx = -2\ln\mathopen{}\left(\left|x-4\right|\right) + \frac{2\tan^{-1}\mathopen{}\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)}{3} +C
